start_here: Say to your AI: "Count the rows of my files index". It runs tool:count-or-copy-your-file-rows at @tools with {"mode":"counts"} and hands back each names-index table with how many rows it holds.
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it reads or fills the tables of your files index in your own database.
instructions: 1. Make sure your database connection (own-rows-postgres-connection) is saved in your vault; the run mounts it by name on descriptor 8 and never prints it.
2. Say to your AI: "Count the rows of my files index" ({"mode":"counts"}); it only reads.

3. To bring an older index in, say: "Copy my files index from /home/example/archive/namespace.sqlite" ({"mode":"copy-archive","from":"/home/example/archive/namespace.sqlite"}); the archive is opened read-only and its ns_* tables are copied into your database.
4. Then ask tool:your-files for your files: list_files answers the copied names.

worked_examples.hands_back: One line per table: ns_name 12, ns_folder 3, ns_file 9 and the rest.
